patch_description: Instead of hoping a local optimizer discovers the right geometry from generic seeds, I directly construct the known D6-symmetric Tammes-14 candidate family (two staggered hexagonal rings at z=±h plus two poles at z=±z0), which is the conjectured optimum matching the reference squared ratio 1/4.165849767 ≈ 0.24005. The family has only two effective degrees of freedom (scale-invariant), so I grid-search and Nelder-Mead-refine (R, h, z0) to maximize the exact ratio. Then I polish with the annealed soft-min/soft-max L-BFGS-B schedule from the prior programs — starting exactly at the symmetric optimum, so the polish only needs to confirm/round it rather than discover it. A few jittered restarts guard against numerical slop, and the best result by true ratio is returned. This is fast (no large multi-seed SLSQP runs) and lands precisely on the symmetric optimum.
